title: Module descent along a connected finite Galois cover
statement:
Let $S$ be a connected scheme [def-pc-scheme], $c:Y\to S$ a connected finite etale Galois cover [def-galois-object], $G=\operatorname{Aut}_S(Y)$ its finite group, and $R$ any commutative ring. Use the small etale site [def-weil-pbc-etale-site], constant sheaves [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf], and module sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. Descent of constant sheaves on $Y$, with their $G$-descent data, gives an additive exact equivalence $T_{c,R}$ between $R$-modules with an $R$-linear $G$-action and the full subcategory of $R_S$-module sheaves $L$ for which $c^{-1}L$ [def-weil-pbc-inverse-image] is constant. It carries trivial actions to constant sheaves and carries finitely generated $R$-modules [def-weil-finitely-generated-module] exactly to the objects of that subcategory locally constant of finite type [def-weil-pbc-locally-constant-finite-type-modules]. Exact means that a sequence on either side is short exact if and only if its corresponding sequence is short exact in modules or ambient module sheaves, respectively. If $R\to A$ is a homomorphism of commutative rings, $N$ is an $A$-module with trivial $G$-action and $V$ an $R$-module with $R$-linear $G$-action, there is a natural $A_S$-linear isomorphism
$$T_{c,A}(N\otimes_R V)\ \cong\ N_S\otimes_{R_S}T_{c,R}(V),$$
where $g(n\otimes v)=n\otimes gv$, module tensors are [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product], and sheaf tensors are [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product]. No finiteness of the underlying sets of $A$, $R$ or $N$ is assumed.

source.place: Expose XVII, Proposition 7.2.3 and the finite quotient identification in the proof of Proposition 7.4.6, pp. 301, 307; module operations and the mixed tensor identification are the corresponding descent operations on constant sheaves.
